headline: Everything you see—and everything you are—is made of atoms too small to see
universal_truth: The invisible underlies the visible; what we can't see creates what we can
fun_facts: A single drop of water contains about 1.5 sextillion atoms—that's 1.5 followed by 21 zeros
Atoms are 99.9999% empty space—you are mostly nothing, held together by forces
Only about 100 different types of atoms create everything in the known universe
discussion_questions: How does knowing you're mostly empty space change your sense of solidity?
What invisible forces hold things together in your life?
Why do only 100 elements create infinite variety?

hook.script: The chair you're sitting on. The air you're breathing. Your own body. Everything is made of the same building blocks—atoms. Too small to see, yet combining in endless ways to create mountains, oceans, stars, and you.

cliff.script: If atoms are the building blocks, how small are they really? And if everything is made of the same basic parts, why do things look and feel so different?
cliff.prompt: What makes different materials different if all are made of atoms?

options.text: Different arrangements and types of atoms create different properties
options.response: Yes. The same few elements, arranged differently, create gold, water, and living tissue.

options.text: Different materials contain completely different types of atoms
options.response: Different elements are used, but the key is arrangement...

fact1.title: Incredibly Small
fact1.script: An atom is so small that a million of them lined up would span a human hair. A single drop of water contains about 1.5 sextillion atoms. You contain roughly 7 octillion atoms—7 followed by 27 zeros. Inconceivable numbers of tiny parts.

fact2.title: Mostly Nothing
fact2.script: Atoms are 99.9999% empty space. If an atom were a football stadium, the nucleus would be a marble at center field. The 'solid' table you touch is actually mostly nothing—held together by electromagnetic forces between atoms.

fact3.title: Only 100 Types
fact3.script: There are only about 100 different types of atoms—the elements on the periodic table. That's it. All the complexity of the universe—every star, every creature, every thought—emerges from combinations of about 100 building blocks.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: The invisible creates the visible. Atoms remind us that what we see and touch emerges from what we cannot perceive. Reality runs deeper than appearances. The building blocks of existence are hidden.

outro.script: That's Day 76. Tomorrow, we'll discover what happens when atoms connect—molecules. Until then, look at your hand and imagine the octillions of atoms making it possible.

growTrack.title: Hidden Foundations - See Beneath the Surface
growTrack.learning_objective: Look for invisible structures that create visible reality
growTrack.activity: Pick something you interact with daily—a relationship, a habit, an organization. What invisible 'atoms' compose it—values, routines, agreements, forces? Understanding what's invisible helps you work with what's visible.
